sources.name: JODI Oil World Database (refinery intake, trade)
IEA Oil Market Report (refinery runs, Hormuz flows)
NBS and customs data for China, via Reuters (refinery runs, imports, output)
EIA monthly crude stocks (checks the US stock figures)

meta.notes: Daily flows are modeled estimates. Monthly official data are shaped by daily shipping signals; no public daily country-level data exist.

nodes.label: Gulf storage
nodes.note: Oil from tanks and idle tankers inside the Gulf. It still has to cross the strait, which is why it flows through Hormuz.

nodes.label: Cargoes at sea
nodes.note: Tankers loaded earlier that reach refiners now. They arrive by sea, with no new production behind them.

nodes.label: Stock draws
nodes.note: Refiners and governments drawing on tanks in their own country, so there is no transit. Part of this band is a balancing residual, largest in March. The Method page has the split.

nodes.label: Cargoes at sea
nodes.note: Oil loaded onto tankers that has not reached a refinery yet.

nodes.label: Stock builds
nodes.note: Oil added to tanks, including Gulf producers storing what they could not ship.

events.label: IRGC closes parts of Hormuz for hours during live-fire drills
US-Israeli strikes on Iran; Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz
events.detail: Tanker transits fall from about 37 a day to about 1 within three weeks. Roughly 15 mb/d of crude used to pass through here.

events.label: Major shipping lines suspend Hormuz transits
Marine insurers cancel Gulf war-risk cover
IEA members agree record 400 mb emergency stock release
events.detail: The largest coordinated release ever, including 172 mb from the US. Deliveries build slowly: US reserves draw 0.7 mb/d in April and 1.3 mb/d in May (EIA).

events.label: Two-week US-Iran ceasefire begins; attacks on ships continue
events.detail: It comes a day after Brent spot peaks at $138. The strait stays nearly shut, and a US blockade of Iran follows on April 13.

events.label: US naval blockade of Iran begins
April: OECD stocks fall about 4 mb/d
events.detail: Government reserves supply 2.3 mb/d of it. Japan's crude imports drop to 0.66 mb/d (JODI) and its tanks fill the gap, while China is still building. Monthly figure, placed mid-month.

events.label: China starts drawing its crude stocks
events.detail: Commercial stocks peaked near 1.25 billion barrels in early May. Refiners then draw about 1 mb/d for three weeks, Vortexa and Kpler estimate, as imports fall.

events.label: May: global stocks fall 143 mb
events.detail: That is 4.6 mb/d, up from 2.5 mb/d in April. OECD government stocks reach their lowest level since 1990. Monthly figure, placed late in the month.

events.label: US-Iran memorandum signed; strait reopens and tankers rush out
events.detail: Tanker counts climb within days, and Brent spot falls toward $70 by late June.

events.label: Gulf exports surge as the strait reopens
events.detail: Gulf oil exports jump 6.5 mb/d in June to 16.1 mb/d, against 24 before the war. Full storage tanks drain, China draws 41 mb, and tanker counts stay high into early July.

events.label: Interim deal collapses; Hormuz shipments near standstill
events.detail: Ships are hit on July 7 and the bump ends. Tanker counts fall from 14 a day to about 2 within two weeks.

events.label: Houthi attack on Saudi tanker threatens Red Sea bypass route
August: China draws again as refineries restart
events.detail: Runs rebound to 13.91 mb/d, the highest since March, while crude available is 13.27 mb/d. That implies a draw of about 0.64 mb/d. Monthly figure, placed mid-month.
